subject: Pilot sizing & deployment economics — recap and next steps
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Park <jason@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot sizing & deployment economics — recap and next steps

Jason — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick written recap and the asks we agreed on so nothing slips between now and the pilot kickoff. Attaching a simple workbook with the numbers below (ACME_pilot_commit_model.xlsx).

Key background (from the call)
- Primary workload: near-real-time chat assistant for warehouse ops (avg. request: 120 tokens prompt, 60 tokens response).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for single-turn requests.
- Security: customer data must be isolated to VPC or dedicated infra for initial pilot; SOC2 evidence requested.
- Expected Q1 pilot volume: 30k requests/day, peak 2.5x burst.

High-level deployment options we walked through
1) Hosted API (Redwood hosted) — fastest to start, per-token billing, automatic autoscale.
2) Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) — capacity reservation with monthly commit, predictable throughput and VPC peering.
3) Private (customer VPC/on‑prem) — full isolation, longer lead time to provision.

Preliminary cost modeling (baseline assumptions)
- Request shape: 120 tokens in, 60 out => 180 tokens total per request.
- Pilot steady volume: 30k req/day => 5.4M tokens/day => ~162M tokens/month (30 day).
- Burst headroom: 2.5x for 2–3 hours/day.

Option A — Hosted API (per-token)
- Assumed rate: $0.00008 per token (generation + overhead)
- Monthly cost = 162,000,000 tokens * $0.00008 = $12,960
- Add buffer for burst autoscale (~+25%) => ~ $16k/month
- Pros: no infra setup, SOC2 evidence available (attached), fastest onboarding.
- Cons: slightly higher unit cost at scale, less control over dedicated GPU locality.

Option B — Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit)
- Example commit: 4x A40-equivalent GPUs reserved + autoscale burst pool.
- Estimated committed monthly fee (list estimate): $9,000/month for base commit (covers steady), incremental burst usage billed at reduced per-minute rates.
- Effective per-token math (steady): $9,000 / 162M tokens = $0.000055/token equivalent.
- When including burst and infra overhead (~+20%), expect ~ $10.8k/month effective.
- Pros: predictable latency, cost advantage at steady state, VPC peering for data isolation.
- Cons: requires a 1–3 month provisioning window for Dedicated pool and minimum commit term.

Option C — Private VPC/on-prem
- Up-front setup / project engineering ~ $40k one-time (networking, infra packaging).
- Ongoing infra ops + support contract estimate ~ $11k/month (for equivalent capacity).
- Pros: full isolation, meets strict regulatory controls.
- Cons: longer lead time, higher initial cost, Redwood support/ops involvement for pilot.

Recommendation for pilot (what we proposed on call)
- Start with a 6-week pilot on Redwood Dedicated (4 GPU commit) with a short hosted fallback during early days to avoid cold start risk.
- Rationale: gives the best balance — meets isolation needs (VPC peering), delivers predictable latency, and shows committed economics vs hosted.
- Pilot asks from Acme: confirm target steady volume and sign a 6-week pilot SOW + commitment estimate so we can schedule the Dedicated pool.

Next steps (agreed)
1) Jason: confirm that the 30k req/day and 2.5x burst assumptions match internal forecasts (reply to this thread).
2) Connor: share the attached pricing workbook with dedicated sizing and a 6-week SOW template (attached).
3) Marissa + Lauren: stand by to accelerate procurement/contract once Acme confirms volumes; will prepare draft MSA amendment for pilot term.

If you prefer starting on Hosted for 2–3 weeks and then switching to Dedicated, we can model the blended cost — I put a toggle in the workbook.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: ACME_pilot_commit_model.xlsx, SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf, pilot-scope-statement.docx

Subject: Re: Pilot sizing & deployment economics — recap and next steps

Connor — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying items from our side before we commit:

1) The 30k/day number is our conservative starting forecast; we could see 45k/day if early user tests go well. Can you model the 45k/day steady case and the blended hosted->dedicated path you mentioned?
2) For dedicated provisioning: what is the minimum commitment term? We have internal procurement constraints that prefer month-to-month or short pilots without long lock-ins.
3) SOC2: contracts@acme.ai needs the SOC2 artifact and a short list of where customer logs are retained. Please confirm retention windows.

If you can send a short table with monthly cost under (30k, 45k) for Hosted vs Dedicated (committed) vs Private, that will help our CFO sign-off. Also include what the expected time to provision Dedicated is (calendar days).

Thanks — will loop in procurement if numbers look reasonable.

—Jason
Jason Park
Head of Product, Acme Robotics
jason@acme.ai | +1 206-555-0199

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, contracts@acme.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing & deployment economics — recap and next steps

Jason — good questions. I updated the attached workbook with the 45k/day steady case and a blended path tab. Summary table below (rounded):

Assumptions used for table: same token shape (180 tokens/request). 30 day months. Dedicated lead time: 10–18 business days to provision pool and complete VPC peering (can be expedited).

Monthly cost estimates (rounded)
- 30k/day (162M tokens/month): Hosted ≈ $16k/month (with burst buffer), Dedicated ≈ $10.8k/month (commit + expected burst charges), Private ≈ $51k first month then $11k/month ops.
- 45k/day (243M tokens/month): Hosted ≈ $24k/month, Dedicated ≈ $15.6k/month, Private ≈ $75k first month then $16k/month ops.

Minimum commitment term for Dedicated pilot: we typically do a 6-week pilot with a short commit that covers that pilot period (no long-term lock if customer wants to evaluate). For enterprise contracts we present 3/6/12 month commit options; pilots are treated separately.

SOC2 / logs: attached SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf (see section 2). Short answers: audit logs retained for 90 days by default in hosted, can be extended for Dedicated/Private with export hooks; customer-requested retention can be supported via log export to customer GCS/S3 for long-term retention.

What I attached in the workbook:
- Per-option monthly breakout (compute, network egress, caching savings)
- Blended onboarding path (Hosted 2 weeks -> Dedicated reserve) with estimated blended cost and a switch plan.
- Pilot SOW draft to speed procurement (pilot scope, success criteria, SLA targets).

If you want, Marissa can prepare a one-page commercial term sheet with pricing and short pilot commitment for procurement to sign. If that looks good, we can target provisioning the Dedicated pool ~10 business days after the signed pilot SOW + PO.

I'll be on PTO Thu-Fri but Marissa will own procurement questions directly.

Connor

On attachments: ACME_pilot_commit_model.xlsx (updated)

Jason / contracts team — looping in procurement on our side. Attached is a concise commercial term sheet for the 6-week Dedicated pilot with the two volume scenarios Connor modeled. Key bullets: 

- Pilot period: 6 weeks (no long-term commitment required beyond pilot).
- Pricing for pilot: listed as a short pilot commit (covers 4 GPU pool + burst buffer); if production conversion occurs we will propose a standard reserved commit.
- PO instructions: send signed SOW + PO number to billing@redwood.ai; we can issue an invoice for the pilot commit.
- Next milestone: once we receive SOW+PO we will schedule provisioning (target 10 business days).

Please confirm if we should proceed with the Dedicated pilot or if you prefer a hybrid start on Hosted for the first two weeks. If you confirm the Dedicated route, Connor will schedule kick-off and engineering onboarding.
